body_markdown:
Colombia has one of the largest diaspora populations in the Americas — over 3 million Colombians live in the US alone. Add to that a fast-growing expat and digital nomad scene in Medellín, Bogotá, and Cartagena, and you've got millions of people sending money from USD to COP every month.


The demand is massive. And the financial industry has historically exploited it.


Here's what actually makes sense in 2026.


---

Let's use a concrete example. You want to send $500 to someone in Colombia — a family member, a contractor, your landlord, or yourself. Here's what each major option actually costs.

---


## 🔍 Breaking Down Each Option


### Western Union


Western Union is the legacy option. It works — their network is huge and reliable. But "works" doesn't mean "cheap."


Their flat fees look manageable until you add the exchange rate margin. Western Union consistently offers rates 2–3% below mid-market. On $500, that's $10–15 gone before you even pay the transfer fee.


For emergencies when nothing else is available, fine. For regular transfers, there's no reason to use it.


### US Bank Wire (SWIFT)


The most expensive option per transfer. Your bank charges $25–45 to send the wire. The recipient's Colombian bank may charge another fee to receive it. And banks use proprietary exchange rates that consistently favor the bank.


On top of that: 2–4 business days. If you need money there today, wires don't help.


### Wise


Wise is a genuine improvement over banks and Western Union. Their fee structure is transparent, and they use the mid-market rate. For USD to COP specifically, Wise charges a percentage fee (around 0.67%) plus a small fixed fee.


The result is a good rate — but not the best. Their percentage fee is higher than Blaze's, and the fixed fee adds up on smaller transfers.


### Blaze


Blaze charges **$1.00 + 1% per transfer to Colombia** — still dramatically cheaper than a bank wire or Western Union. No exchange rate margin. You see exactly what you're paying before you confirm.


Transfers to Colombia arrive instantly via the local payment rails. Whether your recipient banks with Bancolombia, Davivienda, Nequi, or another provider, funds land quickly without extra steps.


---


## 💡 When to Use Each Option


**Use Blaze when:** You want the cheapest, fastest option with no surprises. Works for regular transfers, paying contractors, sending to family, or moving your own money.


**Use Wise when:** You already have an account set up and the transfer amount is large enough that the extra 0.17% doesn't matter to you.


**Use Western Union when:** The recipient needs cash pickup and doesn't have a bank account.


**Use a bank wire when:** Your bank requires it and there's no other option.


---


## 🌆 Common Reasons People Send Money to Colombia


**Supporting family.** The most common use case. Colombian-Americans send billions of pesos home every year. Cutting fees from 3% to around 1.2% is meaningful money over time.


**Paying rent as an expat.** Medellín and Bogotá are full of expats earning USD and paying rent in COP. Monthly rent transfers at $1 + 1% instead of 3%+ saves $20–40/month depending on rent amount.


**Paying contractors.** Developers, designers, virtual assistants — Colombia has a thriving remote workforce. Paying them via Blaze instead of wire saves real money and gets them paid faster.


**Moving money for yourself.** If you're spending time in Colombia and want local currency, Blaze is the cheapest way to convert and transfer your USD.
